app_purpose: Python web framework; django.utils.text.Truncator powers the truncatewords_html / truncatechars_html template filters used to safely shorten user/CMS HTML
root_cause: ReDoS / catastrophic (quadratic, 'linear backtracking') regex behavior in the HTML-truncation word regex re_words = `<[^>]+?>|([^<>\s]+)` used by Truncator._truncate_html (CWE-1333)

v0.ref: PyPI Django==4.2.5 (pre CVE-2023-43665). django/utils/text.py: `re_words = _lazy_re_compile(r'<[^>]+?>|([^<>\s]+)', re.S)`, NO input cap (Truncator has no MAX_LENGTH_HTML). Truncator._truncate_html feeds arbitrary-length text to re_words -> O(n^2) on an open-bracket run.

v1.ref: PyPI Django==4.2.6 (CVE-2023-43665 fix = TARGET). ONLY change to text.py: added `MAX_LENGTH_HTML = 5_000_000` on Truncator and `if len(text) > self.MAX_LENGTH_HTML: text = text[:self.MAX_LENGTH_HTML]` in _truncate_html. The re_words regex is UNCHANGED -> a bracket run WITHIN the 5M cap still backtracks O(n^2). INCOMPLETE FIX.

v2.ref: PyPI Django==4.2.11 (CVE-2024-27351 fix). text.py replaces the re_words regex with a hand-written linear scanner class `WordsRegex` (re_prt=`<|([^<>\s]+)`, re_notag=`([^<>\s]+)`, str.find('>') to close a tag) -> O(n) on open brackets. The 5M cap is retained.

build.strategy: python:3.11-slim, `pip install Django==<DJ_VER> gunicorn==21.2.0` per profile via build-arg DJ_VER (4.2.5/4.2.6/4.2.11). A REAL minimal Django project (app/manage.py + app/proj/{settings,urls,wsgi}.py, NO vendored/edited Django source) is served by gunicorn (1 SYNC worker, --timeout 120). The view POST /truncate reads the untrusted request body and calls the REAL installed Django's django.utils.text.Truncator(text).words(30, html=True) -- the exact sink behind the `truncatewords_html` template filter. The ReDoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request and observed as SERVER-SIDE response latency.
build.host_safety: each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=512m so a catastrophic O(n^2) match is CPU-throttled (flat memory; short/bounded payloads). gunicorn --timeout 120 keeps the worker alive past the oracle's 10s HTTP read timeout so the latency is MEASURED, not worker-killed. The oracle restarts (kill+up) a fresh gunicorn before every probe so a wedged sync worker never poisons the next measurement. DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE=None lets the ~5MB original payload reach the view body (a truncation service intentionally accepts large HTML). Payload lengths: original 5,030,000 chars, residual 30,000 chars, benign 840 chars.

flag.resource: server-side truncation CPU of a REAL Django app: POST /truncate -> django.utils.text.Truncator(text).words(30, html=True) inside a gunicorn sync worker, on attacker-supplied HTML
flag.placement: no canary/token; signal = SERVER-SIDE HTTP response latency of an EXTERNAL POST /truncate request (10s client read timeout)
flag.detect: DoS iff HTTP latency > T_SLOW (2000ms) or read-timeout; bounded iff < T_SLOW; benign fast iff < T_FAST (300ms)

mechanism.summary: Truncator._truncate_html tokenizes HTML with `regex.search(text, pos)` in a loop, where regex = re_words = `<[^>]+?>|([^<>\s]+)` (re.S). On a run of open brackets '<<<...<' (no '>'), at every start position the first alternative `<[^>]+?>` matches '<' then lazily expands `[^>]+?` scanning to end-of-string for a '>' that never comes (each '<' satisfies `[^>]`), fails, and the second alternative `[^<>\s]+` is excluded by '<' -- so search advances one position and repeats the full O(n) scan => O(n^2) catastrophic (Django release notes: the regex 'still exhibited linear backtracking complexity'). CVE-2019-14232 (2019) first rewrote this regex; CVE-2023-43665 (4.2.6) did NOT touch the regex and instead capped input to MAX_LENGTH_HTML=5,000,000 chars -- but O((5M)^2) is still catastrophic, so any bracket run within the cap still DoSes (INCOMPLETE FIX). CVE-2024-27351 (4.2.11) finally replaced the regex with the linear WordsRegex scanner (uses str.find('>') to close a tag instead of a backtracking quantifier).
mechanism.original_sink: re_words regex in Truncator._truncate_html (django/utils/text.py) -- reached with NO length bound on 4.2.5
mechanism.residual_sink: SAME re_words regex in Truncator._truncate_html -- reached with a payload WITHIN the 5M cap on 4.2.6 (cap does not bound quadratic-within-cap)
mechanism.guard_line_v1: MAX_LENGTH_HTML = 5_000_000 ; if len(text) > self.MAX_LENGTH_HTML: text = text[: self.MAX_LENGTH_HTML]   # CVE-2023-43665: input cap ONLY; re_words regex unchanged
mechanism.guard_line_v2: class WordsRegex: ... re_prt=_lazy_re_compile(r'<|([^<>\s]+)', re.S); re_notag=_lazy_re_compile(r'([^<>\s]+)', re.S); end=text.find('>', partial.end(0))   # CVE-2024-27351: linear scanner replaces the backtracking regex

regex_evolution.v1_4.2.6: re_words = _lazy_re_compile(r'<[^>]+?>|([^<>\s]+)', re.S)   # UNCHANGED; added MAX_LENGTH_HTML=5_000_000 cap
regex_evolution.v2_4.2.11: re_words = WordsRegex  (linear scanner; old regex kept only as a comment)

mechanism.original_redos_payload: '\t' * 5_000_000 + '<' * 30_000  (len 5,030,000) -- the O(n^2) open-bracket run lives BEYOND the 5M cap; the within-cap prefix is cheap whitespace. 4.2.5 (no cap) processes the bracket tail -> slow; 4.2.6 truncates text to the first 5M (whitespace only) -> bounded.
mechanism.residual_redos_payload: '<' * 30_000  (len 30,000) -- open-bracket run entirely WITHIN the 5M cap. Backtracks O(n^2) on re_words on BOTH 4.2.5 and 4.2.6 (the cap never triggers); linear on 4.2.11's WordsRegex. Same shape as Django's own CVE-2024-27351 regression test `test = '<' * 60_000`.
mechanism.benign_payload:
'

Joel is a slug

' * 40 (len 840) -- well-formed HTML that exercises the words+tags code path; fast on all versions.
